title: moe-proxy refuses to bridge to a daemon whose /health reports another project
description:
Split from task-e7f4026a (HIGH, human-reported, recurring). That row keeps the moe-agent.sh/.ps1 pre-flight slice and the final verification of all three slices, and it dependsOn this task.

Objective: moe-proxy checks which project the daemon it is about to bridge actually serves.
- Today readDaemonInfoResult (packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts) compares only the projectPath written in .moe/daemon.json with its own project. A stale file always matches, so after a project's daemon dies, the proxy bridges to whatever daemon now holds that port.
- On 2026-10-30 a px4swarm seat registered with the moes daemon this way, then claimed and coded a moes task.
- Every wrapper RPC also goes through this proxy: moe_rpc and Invoke-MoeRpc spawn it one-shot. So this check alone stops a seat from registering or claiming on a foreign daemon.

Deliverable:
- A new packages/moe-proxy/src/daemonIdentity.ts.
  - It GETs http://<getDaemonHost()>:<port>/health with a bounded timeout and a body capped at 64 KiB.
  - It classifies the reply as same, foreign (with the served projectPath) or unknown.
  - It compares paths with comparableProjectPath from utils.ts, the rule the daemon's own probeDaemonHealth uses (D:\x == D:/x == /mnt/d/x).
  - It imports utils.ts but does not edit it: task-a4ad3fdb and task-724e31fa edit that file.
- packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts connect() runs the probe before it opens /mcp, on every connect and reconnect.
  - Foreign: write an error naming both projects and the fix, then exit 1. That is the same class as today's 'daemon.json belongs to a different project'. The fix is: this project's .moe/daemon.json is stale; restart this project's daemon, which takes the next free port. The proxy never opens /mcp.
  - Unknown: proceed exactly as today, so the reconnect path and older daemons keep working. Unknown covers an unreachable /health, a timeout, a non-JSON or oversize body, and a reply with no projectPath from an older daemon.
- Tests:
  - packages/moe-proxy/src/daemonIdentity.test.ts, against a real local http server;
  - one end-to-end case that spawns the proxy against a fake daemon whose /health names another project, and asserts exit 1, the message, and that no /mcp upgrade arrived.

Not in scope:
- daemon code: there is no wire change, and a project parameter on the upgrade is deferred hardening;
- moe-agent.sh/.ps1 (task-e7f4026a);
- the JetBrains plugin (a sibling task);
- the proxy README and utils.ts.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0): cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test. From WSL, run it in a Linux-native snapshot, because the checkout's node_modules are Windows builds (mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate).
definitionOfDone: connect() probes the daemon's /health before opening /mcp, on every connect and reconnect. When the reply's projectPath is another project by comparableProjectPath, the proxy exits 1 with an error naming both projects and telling the reader to restart this project's daemon, and it makes no /mcp upgrade. Proven by an end-to-end test against a fake daemon.

This project spelled D:\x, D:/x or /mnt/d/x connects as before. An unreachable /health, a timeout, a non-JSON or oversize body, and a reply without projectPath all keep today's behavior. Proven by daemonIdentity.test.ts rows.
packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts is unchanged; the diff is daemonIdentity.ts, its tests and index.ts.
`cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test` exits 0, with its output supplied to complete_task.

M8 is a known gap, checked against the code. The first probe runs before the stdin reader exists, so nothing is pending and a signal's gracefulShutdown exits at once (:319-323). The 'close' handler does not reconnect after shutdown (:500). So the guard is reached only when shutdown starts during a RECONNECT probe with messages queued. The guard then opens no socket, and the queued messages get the existing 'still queued' error at gracefulShutdown's 2 s cap. Without the guard, the new socket would flush them. That window is narrow and the process is exiting anyway. No test was added; the plan adds one only if QA requires it. There were no unexpected survivors.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of `git show 4f2d53dd -- packages/moe-proxy/src`. No genuine defect was found, so no bytes changed.
(1) The probe settles exactly once on every path. finish() has a done guard, clears the timer and calls req?.destroy(). A late end/aborted/error, or the 'error' that destroy() itself causes, hits the guard. Every req and res stream has an 'error' listener, so no unhandled error event. A synchronous http.request throw is caught with req still null, so destroy is a no-op and the result is unknown. connect()'s .catch is the same as main().catch. The probe registers only per-request http listeners, nothing on process or stdin, and the stdin once-guard (:556) is unchanged.
(2) The cap counts Buffer chunk bytes; no setEncoding is set on res. The exact-cap test body is ASCII, so a chars-for-bytes mutant would survive. That is harmless: either count bounds memory.
(3) http.request gets `hostname` from getDaemonHost() and the port from daemon.json. A bare IPv6 MOE_DAEMON_HOST works for the probe. The older ws URL still needs brackets, which ends in exit 1 as before, via .catch instead of main().catch. The 1.5 s overall timer also bounds DNS.
(4) Only the served path goes through displayServedPath. Our own projectPath is printed as is.
(5) One connect means one probe, one .then and at most one openDaemonSocket. Nothing else schedules connect() while a probe is in flight: stale-socket closes are ignored, and the close handler returns early once shuttingDown is set (:500). The foreign branch exits before any upgrade (E1, E1b, E3). M8 is the untested shutdown-during-reconnect window (step 2).
(6) An unknown result opens the socket as before (M3 is killed by E4 and 13 index e2e cases). The only change is up to 1.5 s of probe latency. Stdin stays paused and buffered until the reader is attached.
(7) No false 'foreign' for the owner daemon. daemon.json and /health come from the same variable (daemon index.ts:789 and :709), and the proxy compares both with the same comparableProjectPath. So any daemon that passes readDaemonInfoResult classifies as 'same', symlinks included. A relative served path is 'unknown'. /health costs only in-memory map sizes (StateManager.getStats).
Documented limits, unchanged:
- TOCTOU between /health and /mcp; the hardening is deferred.
- A foreign daemon on reconnect is fatal, as the DoD mandates. Re-reading daemon.json and retrying would survive an own-daemon port move; that is out of scope.
- On Windows, writeError followed by exit(1) mirrors the existing daemon.json-mismatch path at :373-374.
- NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY routing makes the probe 'unknown', which fails open.
Size notes: daemonIdentity.test.ts is 302 lines, 2 over the role's 300-line soft cap. This round is no-byte, so it stays as is. openDaemonSocket is the old connect() body moved verbatim.

implementationPlan.description:
Create packages/moe-proxy/src/daemonIdentity.ts.

Exports:
- `export type DaemonIdentity = { kind: 'same' } | { kind: 'foreign'; projectPath: string } | { kind: 'unknown' };`
- `export async function probeDaemonIdentity(host: string, port: number, projectPath: string, options: { timeoutMs?: number } = {}): Promise<DaemonIdentity>`. The default timeoutMs is 1500, a named const; /health is local and answers in milliseconds.
- `export const MAX_HEALTH_BODY_BYTES = 64 * 1024`.

Behavior:
- One node:http GET of http://<host>:<port>/health, with a hostname option; a bare IPv6 literal works without brackets.
- One overall timer that destroys the request, plus the request's own timeout.
- Byte-counted reads: destroy and answer unknown once the total exceeds MAX_HEALTH_BODY_BYTES.
- Settle exactly once, through a `done` guard.
- Answer:
  - statusCode 200, a JSON object (not an array), and a non-empty string projectPath: 'same' when comparableProjectPath(reply) === comparableProjectPath(projectPath), else {kind:'foreign', projectPath: reply};
  - everything else is 'unknown'.
- Never reject. Every error, timeout or parse failure resolves {kind:'unknown'}.
- Clear the timer and destroy the socket on every path. Import comparableProjectPath from './utils.js', and do NOT edit utils.ts: task-a4ad3fdb and task-724e31fa edit it.

Add a header comment on why the probe exists. A stale daemon.json always matches its own project, so a port reused by another project's daemon would be bridged (task-e7f4026a). Unknown keeps today's behavior for older daemons and the reconnect path.

Run daemonIdentity.test.ts group A green.

amendments.description:
Create packages/moe-proxy/src/daemonIdentity.ts.

Exports:
- `export type DaemonIdentity = { kind: 'same' } | { kind: 'foreign'; projectPath: string } | { kind: 'unknown' };`
- `export async function probeDaemonIdentity(host: string, port: number, projectPath: string, options: { timeoutMs?: number } = {}): Promise<DaemonIdentity>`. The default timeoutMs is 1500, a named const; /health is local and answers in milliseconds.
- `export const MAX_HEALTH_BODY_BYTES = 64 * 1024`.

Behavior:
- One node:http GET of http://<host>:<port>/health, using the hostname option, so a bare IPv6 literal works without brackets.
- One overall timer that destroys the request, plus the request's own timeout.
- Count bytes as they are read. Once the total exceeds MAX_HEALTH_BODY_BYTES, destroy the request and answer unknown.
- Settle exactly once, through a `done` guard.

Classification, shared with JetBrains task-90664db1:
- Accept only statusCode 200 or 503 (the daemon's healthy and unhealthy /health codes).
- The body must parse as a JSON object, not an array.
- projectPath must be a non-empty ABSOLUTE string: a drive letter (/^[a-zA-Z]:[\\/]/), UNC (starting with two backslashes) or POSIX (starting with '/'). Write it as a small exported isAbsoluteAnyOs(), not path.isAbsolute, which on Linux rejects 'D:\\x'.
- Then: 'same' when comparableProjectPath(reply) === comparableProjectPath(projectPath), else {kind:'foreign', projectPath: reply}.
- Everything else is 'unknown': a relative projectPath (the daemon reports its raw --project argument), any other status, and any error, timeout or parse failure.

Never reject. Clear the timer and destroy the socket on every path. Import comparableProjectPath from './utils.js', and do NOT edit utils.ts (task-a4ad3fdb and task-724e31fa edit it).

Header comment: why the probe exists. A stale daemon.json always matches its own project, so a port reused by another project's daemon would be bridged (task-e7f4026a). 'unknown' keeps today's behavior for older daemons and for the reconnect path.

Run daemonIdentity.test.ts group A until it is green.
amendments.reason: This step adopts the shared classification rule: 200 or 503 with an absolute projectPath; a relative path or any other status is unknown. That keeps the proxy and the JetBrains sibling (task-90664db1) identical. Without it, an unhealthy foreign daemon (503) would be bridged, and a relative --project could be misread as foreign.
